rationale_summary: EO 14365 is dominantly framed around economic_competitiveness, justifying federal preemption of State AI statutes as essential to sustain global AI dominance, attract trillions of dollars in investment, and win the AI race. Economic_competitiveness narrowly edges out innovation_enablement because removing the 50-state compliance patchwork and burdensome regulation is explicitly framed as the means to achieve global supremacy against foreign adversaries. Innovation_enablement is a close secondary frame emphasizing start-up compliance relief and a minimally burdensome national standard, accompanied by national_security (explicit race with adversaries for supremacy), and secondary references to fundamental_rights (First Amendment and anti-censorship) and consumer_public_safety (child safety protections).

evidence_spans.quote: It is the policy of the United States to sustain and enhance the United States' global AI dominance through a minimally burdensome national policy framework for AI.
A carefully crafted national framework can ensure that the United States wins the AI race, as we must.

To win, United States AI companies must be free to innovate without cumbersome regulation. But excessive State regulation thwarts this imperative. First, State-by-State regulation by definition creates a patchwork of 50 different regulatory regimes that makes compliance more challenging, particularly for start-ups.
United States leadership in Artificial Intelligence (AI) will promote United States national and economic security and dominance across many domains.
But we remain in the earliest days of this technological revolution and are in a race with adversaries for supremacy within it.
That framework should also ensure that children are protected, censorship is prevented, copyrights are respected, and communities are safeguarded.
